primary_meaning: The kingdom of heaven (or the gospel of salvation/Christ) as a treasure of supreme, inestimable worth for which everything else should be sacrificed
primary_basis: Matthew 13:45-46 (Parable of the Pearl of Great Price)

alternatives.meaning: Sacred or holy things (divine truths, the gospel, or teachings of Christ) that must not be cast before the unworthy or unappreciative
The Church or the individual human soul (in readings where the merchant is Christ/God who seeks and purchases the pearl at great cost)
Purity, perfection, or the glorious entrance into the heavenly city
General preciousness, rarity, or wisdom formed through trial
basis: Broader biblical imagery of pearls as costly jewels (e.g., Job 28; 1 Timothy 2:9; Revelation 17–18)

notes: The parable supplies the dominant Christian symbolic association; secondary uses (Matt 7:6; Rev 21) are also standard. Allegorical details of the parable (who is the merchant, what exactly is the pearl) vary by tradition but do not displace the core sense of supreme value.
